text:
Maria: FYI customer Quokka opened a high-priority ticket — intermittent 5xx/504 from hosted inference (api.redwood.com/v1/generate). Started ~09:30 UTC and is ongoing. Partial logs attached in ticket #5371.

Kevin: repro snippet from their environment (got 504 consistently):
```bash
curl -v -X POST \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate\" \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-hosted-1","input":"hello world","max_tokens":256}'
```

ingress-alerts: ALERT: hosted-gateway-us-east queue_depth=98% (threshold=90%) continuous_batcher_backlog=5200 tail_timeouts=~4/min 

Samir: oncall — ack. Pulling traces now. Maria, can you paste a trace-id or session-id from the ticket? Also any recent deploys?

Maria: trace_id=trc_0a9f3e (from support logs). No customer-side deploys reported. We rolled small routing tweak at 07:40 but it was low-risk.

Zhen: looking at metrics — batcher backlog on hostpool hgp-us-east-1 spiked at 09:28, continuous-batching queue length grew past batcher_queue_limit (1024) and we started dropping/timeouting tails. KV-cache warmups increased latencies so backlog snowballed.

Kevin: here's the client-side timeline: first successful requests, then a cluster of 5xxs for ~18m then intermittent success. Their token counts are normal.

Samir: quick checks I ran:
```bash
# check gateway pods for restarts
kubectl -n hosted get pods -l app=hosted-gateway -o wide
# gateway health endpoint
curl -s http://gateway-internal.us-east/health | jq .queue_depth
```
Gateway pods healthy, no restarts. Health endpoint shows queue_depth=980/1000 for one noisy hostpool.

Zhen: digging deeper into batcher. continuous-batcher backlog by host: hgp-a:1200, hgp-b:1400, hgp-c:2600 — total ~5200. The scheduler is trying to keep latency SLO for in-flight small requests but prefix caching thrash made per-request time blow up, batches get huge and dequeue stalls.

Maria: customer alarm: "calls fail with 504, then succeed minutes later". They're escalating to SOC. Can we provide a mitigation ASAP?

Samir: immediate mitigations: 1) enable temporary adaptive-shed on the affected hostpool to reject large/cheap requests instead of letting them queue; 2) reduce max_batch_size for continuous-batcher on hgp-us-east to force more aggressive flushes; 3) route critical customers to spare hostpool if capacity exists.

Zhen: I can toggle adaptive-shed and reduce batch_size. Command I will run in ~5m:
```bash
# patch hostpool config (k8s configmap / control plane API)
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://control-plane.internal/api/hostpools/hgp-us-east/config \n  -d '{"adaptive_shed":true,"continuous_batch_max_batch":32}'
```
This should drop backlog growth and produce immediate tail-latency relief. Will watch metrics for 10m.

ingress-alerts: Event: adaptive_shed toggled=true on hgp-us-east by Zhen at 1765554370 

Kevin: passing interim mitigation note to Quokka support. They asked for ETA on full resolution.

Samir: timeline — toggle now, watch 10m; if backlog decreases we'll keep and then plan a rollout of smaller batch config across region and a follow-up change to prefix/KV cache priming to avoid cold thrash.

Zhen: toggle done. Early signal: backlog dropped from 5200 -> ~900 in ~90s, tail_timeouts down to 0.8/min. P95 request latency dropped from 1.9s -> 0.45s on the noisy hostpool.

Maria: relaying to customer: initial mitigation applied and customer seeing fewer 5xx; keeping them updated.

Samir: action items:
- Samir: create incident doc + postmortem link (I'll own)
- Zhen: follow up with root cause (why kv-cache priming thrash at 09:28) and propose cache warmup or conservative quantization profile for noisy customers.
- Kevin: confirm with Quokka that errors stopped and log any remaining traces in ticket #5371.

Kevin: customer confirmed reduced failures after ~2min. Asking for postmortem timeline and whether this could recur.

Zhen: I'll run an evaulation harness against traffic pattern to reproduce the kv-warmup cascade and attach config diffs for safe rollout.

Samir: excellent. Leaving the adaptive-shed enabled for 1 hour and we will revert if stable. Will pop an update in #incidents when PM/CS comms ready.

Maria: thanks all. Marking as active incident; assigning severity P2 for now (customer impact but mitigation up).

ingress-alerts: NOTE: followup anomaly detection ticket created id=anomaly_8921 for hostpool cold-cache thrash detection.
